stories.headline: US hits 80+ Iranian targets, Iran strikes Gulf bases, Trump declares ceasefire deal 'over'

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said it completed a new round of offensive strikes against Iran on July 7, hitting more than 80 targets with precision munitions, including air defence systems, command-and-control networks, coastal radar sites, anti-ship missile capabilities and more than 60 IRGC small boats in and near the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: "U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) forces completed a new round of offensive strikes against Iran, July 7, hitting over 80 targets with precision munitions as an immediate response to Iran's latest attacks on commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz."

key_facts.fact: The strikes answered attacks on three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz: the Marshall Islands-flagged M/T Al Rekayyat (a Qatari LNG carrier), the Saudi-flagged M/T Wedyan and the Liberia-flagged M/T Cyprus Prosperity.
key_facts.excerpt: The US said the operation was in response to attacks on three commercial ships — the Marshall Islands-flagged M/T Al Rekayyat, Saudi Arabia-flagged M/T Wedyan and Liberia-flagged M/T Cyprus Prosperity — while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Hours before the strikes, the US Treasury revoked General License X — issued June 22 under the US-Iran memorandum of understanding, and valid through August 21 — replacing it with General License X1, which bars new purchases or shipments of Iranian oil after July 7 and allows only wind-down transactions through July 17.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury downgraded the waiver on July 7 in response to Tehran's aggression and issued General License X1 revoking those authorities. It no longer permits new purchases, loading, or shipments of Iranian oil after July 7. Instead, only transactions necessary to complete deals already authorized under General License X through July 17 are allowed.

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday July 8 Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it carried out a joint missile and drone operation against 85 US military sites, including Bandar Salman and Bahrain's Fifth Naval District and Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, and said it shot down a US MQ-9 drone.
key_facts.excerpt: the IRGC said it carried out a joint missile and drone operation against 85 key US military sites in Bandar Salman, Bahrain's Fifth Naval District and Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, and shot down a US MQ9 drone attempting to interfere in the operation.

key_facts.fact: Air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain, home to the US Navy's 5th Fleet, and in Kuwait, whose army said its air defences were confronting 'hostile' missile and drone attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: The extent of the damage, if any, was not immediately clear, but the Kuwait Army confirmed in a statement that its air defenses were confronting "hostile missile and drone attacks."

key_facts.fact: Asked at the NATO summit in Ankara whether the interim memorandum of understanding reached in June was over, Trump said: 'To me, I think it's over. I don't want to deal with them,' calling Iran's leadership 'scum'. Oil prices rose to a two-week high.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked before a NATO summit in Turkey whether the memorandum of understanding reached last month was over, Trump said: "It's a very interesting question. To me, I think it's over. I don't want to deal with them." ... In a flare-up of hostilities that pushed oil prices up to a two-week high, Iran said it had targeted U.S. military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait.

key_facts.fact: Iran's chief negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused Washington of 'major MoU violations', citing persistent threats of further strikes, the reinstatement of oil sanctions and attacks on southern Iran. The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes.
key_facts.excerpt: Mohammad Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator, called the reinstatement of oil sanctions "major MoU violations" by the US, citing "attacks on southern Iran" as further violations.

key_facts.fact: The US strikes came on the day huge crowds mourned Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in the holy city of Qom; indirect talks in Qatar had ended the previous week with no headway.
key_facts.excerpt: After a day in which huge crowds mourned Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in the holy city of Qom, U.S. Central Command said it completed strikes that hit over 80 targets... The ceasefire was intended to provide a 60-day window for negotiations on a permanent agreement, but indirect talks in Qatar ended last week with no sign of headway.

stories.headline: NATO leaders meet in Ankara, pledging 70 billion euros in 2026 military aid to Ukraine

key_facts.fact: NATO's 32 member states opened a two-day summit in Ankara on July 7; leaders are due to formally endorse the Ankara Declaration on July 8 at a North Atlantic Council session chaired by Erdogan and Secretary General Mark Rutte.
key_facts.excerpt: NATO leaders from the alliance's 32 member states opened a two-day summit in Ankara, Türkiye, on 7 July, with US President Donald Trump set to hold a bilateral meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines

key_facts.fact: The draft declaration commits allies to $80 billion (70 billion euros) in military equipment, aid and training for Ukraine in 2026, with a goal of at least an equivalent level in 2027. The US is not expected to contribute funding.
key_facts.excerpt: NATO allies are set to confirm commitments to provide $80 billion (€70 billion) in military equipment, aid and training for Ukraine's defense forces in 2026, and to affirm a goal of maintaining at least an equivalent level of assistance in 2027, Reuters reports. The US is not expected to provide funding toward this aid.

key_facts.fact: European allies and Canada spent $90 billion more on defence in real terms in 2025 than in 2024, taking total spending above $570 billion — a roughly 20% increase in one year, according to Rutte. The declaration notes a $159 billion (139 billion euro) increase in defence investment.
key_facts.excerpt: NATO's European members and Canada spent $90 billion more on defence in real terms in 2025 than in 2024, bringing total spending to more than $570 billion — an increase of around 20 per cent in a single year, Rutte said last month. A draft of the summit's final declaration reviewed by Reuters journalists states that European allies will note they increased their defense investment by $159 billion (€139 billion) together with Canada.

key_facts.fact: Allies announced large procurement contracts at the summit: a new fleet of transport aircraft from Airbus, and Sweden's GlobalEye planes to replace NATO's ageing AWACS early-warning fleet. The Netherlands alone said it would announce deals worth more than $3.43 billion, including air defence with Belgium and naval ships with Britain.
key_facts.excerpt: Large contracts have been announced for a new fleet of transport aircraft to be built by Airbus. Nato's ageing fleet of AWACS (Airborne Warning and Control System) early warning aircraft are to be replaced by Sweden's GlobeEye planes.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky told the summit that Europe needs its own mass-produced anti-ballistic systems and missiles, and that the work 'cannot wait until 2030 or beyond'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Europe needs its own effective anti-ballistic system and missiles" said President Zelensky. ... "And this work is already under way and I urge you and all of our partners to give it the attention it deserves. And this cannot wait until 2030 or beyond, Europe needs affordable mass-produced anti-ballistic systems as soon as possible."

key_facts.fact: On the sidelines on July 7, Canada announced more than $900 million in new military aid for Ukraine, and Ukraine signed drone co-production and defence cooperation agreements with Estonia, Denmark and the Netherlands.
key_facts.excerpt: Canada announced more than $900 million in new military aid for Ukraine on July 7... Ukraine signed major defense cooperation agreements with Estonia, Denmark, and the Netherlands under the Drone Deal framework, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on July 7.

key_facts.fact: At last year's summit members agreed to raise the target to 5% of GDP: 3.5% on core military spending by 2035 plus 1.5% on security-related needs. On the eve of the Ankara summit Trump called Germany's defence spending 'ridiculous'.
key_facts.excerpt: At the NATO summit last year, members agreed to increase their target to 5 percent of GDP: 3.5 percent on military spending by 2035 and 1.5 percent on security-related needs. ... On the eve of the summit, Trump called Germany's defence spending "ridiculous".

stories.headline: Trump says US will lift CAATSA sanctions on Turkiye and will consider selling it F-35s

key_facts.fact: Meeting Erdogan at his presidential compound in Ankara on July 7, Trump said Washington will remove the sanctions imposed on Turkiye's defence sector: 'We're going to be taking the sanctions off. It's time. We don't want to sanction friends.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're going to be taking the sanctions off," Trump told reporters just before his meeting with Erdogan during a visit to Turkey for a NATO summit. "It's time. We don't want to sanction friends," he said, adding that his Secretary of State and Treasury Secretary were working on the issue.

key_facts.fact: The sanctions were imposed in 2020 under the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) after Turkiye acquired Russian S-400 air defence systems in 2019; they targeted Turkiye's Presidency of Defence Industries and included US export-licence bans plus financial and banking restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: The pivot comes after the US booted Turkiye from the F-35 programme after Ankara acquired Russian S-400 air defence systems in 2019. Washington also imposed sanctions under the so-called Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA). ... The CAATSA sanctions, meanwhile, specifically targeted Turkiye's Presidency of Defence Industries and included US export license bans as well as financial and banking restrictions.

key_facts.fact: On the F-35, Trump said 'It's a decision we're going to make... it's a great plane, the best plane by far and it's certainly something we will consider,' adding that Turkey 'has been, in many ways, much more loyal than other countries'.
key_facts.excerpt: "It's a decision we're going to make," Trump said as he met Turkish President Recep Erdogan at Erdogan's presidential compound. "We have a better relationship with Turkey, and Turkey's been, in many ways, much more loyal than other countries that we think would be loyal," Trump said.

key_facts.fact: Jet sales remain blocked by US law: Congress passed legislation in late 2019 barring F-35 transfers to Turkiye while it retains the S-400, and Section 1245 of the FY2020 NDAA requires executive certification before any transfer.
key_facts.excerpt: While the president has authority over sanctions policy, Congress enacted additional restrictions after Turkey's purchase of the S-400. Section 1245 of the fiscal year 2020 National Defense Authorization Act bars the transfer of F-35 aircraft to Turkey unless the executive branch certifies that Ankara has met statutory requirements related to the Russian missile system.

key_facts.fact: Erdogan said Turkiye had been 'promised five jets' and that he expected a favourable decision to emerge from the Ankara summit.
key_facts.excerpt: "We have been promised five jets," the Turkish president said, adding that he expected the issue to move "in a positive course" during the NATO summit.

key_facts.fact: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pressed Washington not to resume F-35 sales, telling Fox News on Monday that they would 'upset the power balance in the Middle East'.
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking on Monday to Fox News, Netanyahu said the sale of F-35s to Turkiye would "upset the power balance in the Middle East, which is ultimately guaranteed by Israeli air superiority"

stories.headline: South Korea's Kospi enters a bear market, down over 20% from its June record on AI-chip doubts

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday July 8 the Kospi fell 5.17% to 7,260.55 as of 0519 GMT, a third straight losing session, leaving it more than 20% below its record close of 9,114.55 on June 22 — the conventional threshold confirming a bear market.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark KOSPI was down 395.76 points, or 5.17%, at 7,260.55 as of 0519 GMT. That means it has dropped more than 20% from a record close of 9,114.55 hit on June 22, a threshold commonly considered to confirm that a market is in bearish territory.

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday July 7 the index closed down 4.91% at 7,656.31 after falling as much as 8.07% intraday to 7,401.56, triggering a 20-minute market-wide circuit breaker — the sixth this year and the 12th in the market's history.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 7, the Korea Exchange reported that the KOSPI closed at 7,656.31, down 395.02 points (4.91%)... at 1:51:33 p.m., the KOSPI fell to 7,401.56, marking an 8.07% drop from the previous day, prompting the Korea Exchange to activate the first-stage circuit breaker.

key_facts.fact: The rout was set off by profit-taking after Samsung Electronics guided to a second-quarter operating profit of 8.9 trillion won, above the 8.4 trillion won consensus; Samsung fell 6.92% on July 7 and SK Hynix 6.06%.
key_facts.excerpt: Technology stocks plunged on profit-taking after Samsung Electronics estimated its operating profit for the April-June period at 89.4 trillion won, beating market forecasts. ... Market bellwether Samsung Electronics plunged 6.92 percent to 296,000 won, while chip giant SK hynix declined 6.06 percent to 2,201,000 won.

key_facts.fact: Selling continued on July 8 after US semiconductor stocks slumped overnight, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping 4.7% as investors questioned whether AI-related spending could be sustained. Samsung fell a further 6.25% and SK Hynix 3.59%.
key_facts.excerpt: Chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 6.25% and peer SK Hynix lost 3.59%, after U.S. semiconductor stocks slumped overnight, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping 4.7% as investors questioned whether AI-related spending could be sustained.

key_facts.fact: Foreign investors net sold 3.3 trillion won (about $2.16 billion) of Korean shares on July 7, while individuals net bought 3.13 trillion won. Despite the losses the Kospi was still up 76% for the year at that point.
key_facts.excerpt: Foreign investors were net sellers of shares worth 3.3 trillion won, equivalent to about US$2.16 billion, adding pressure on the market. ... Despite Tuesday's steep losses, the KOSPI remains up 76% since the start of the year, driven largely by the strong rally in semiconductor stocks.

key_facts.fact: Two heavyweight non-chip names amplified the fall: LG Energy Solution slid 8.74% after warning second-quarter operating profit would drop 77% on weaker EV battery demand, and shipbuilder Hanwha Ocean plunged 24.29% after Canada picked German submarines over its bid.
key_facts.excerpt: LG Energy Solution slid 8.74% after warning that second-quarter operating profit is expected to plunge 77% due to weaker electric vehicle battery demand. Shipbuilder Hanwha Ocean plunged 24.29% after Canada selected German submarines over South Korean bids in a major defence contract.

key_facts.fact: South Korea's Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol pledged to closely monitor risk factors amid worries about newly introduced single-stock leveraged ETFs linked to chipmaker stocks.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea's Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol pledged to closely monitor risk factors that could heighten stock market volatility, on worries about recently introduced single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) linked to chipmaker stocks.

stories.headline: FDA approves Vera's Trutakna, the first dual BAFF/APRIL drug for IgA nephropathy

key_facts.fact: On July 7, 2026 Vera Therapeutics announced the FDA granted TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj) accelerated approval to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary IgA nephropathy at risk of disease progression.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 7, 2026, Vera Therapeutics, Inc. issued a press release announcing that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj) accelerated approval to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy at risk for disease progression.

key_facts.fact: Trutakna is the first US drug that inhibits both BAFF (B-cell activating factor) and APRIL (a proliferation-inducing ligand), two cytokines involved in B-cell survival and the autoantibodies that drive IgA nephropathy. Vera in-licensed atacicept from Merck KGaA about six years ago.
key_facts.excerpt: Atacicept, a recombinant fusion protein to be marketed under the brand name Trutakna, is now the first drug in the U.S. that inhibits both B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), two cytokines involved in B-cell survival and the production of autoantibodies associated with IgAN.

key_facts.fact: The accelerated approval rests on an interim analysis of the phase 3 Origin 3 trial, which showed a statistically significant 42% reduction in urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio versus placebo at week 36. Confirmatory data are expected in the third quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Trutakna's accelerated approval is supported by data from an interim analysis of the phase 3 Origin 3 trial, which linked the drug to a statistically significant 42% reduction in UPCR compared with placebo at week 36.

key_facts.fact: Trutakna is the sixth drug approved for IgA nephropathy in the US, after Calliditas' Tarpeyo (2021), Travere's Filspari, Novartis' Vanrafia and Fabhalta, and Otsuka's Voyxact (late 2025). Vertex's rival povetacicept has an FDA decision date of Nov. 30, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA doled out its first IgAN approval to Calliditas Therapeutics' corticosteroid Tarpeyo in 2021. Since then, the agency has cleared a dual endothelin angiotensin receptor antagonist in Travere Therapeutics' Filspari, plus Novartis' endothelin A receptor blocker Vanrafia and complement inhibitor Fabhalta. Otsuka's Voyxact, which targets APRIL alone, reached the market toward the end of 2025. ... Vertex Pharmaceuticals' povetacicept has posted a 49.8% reduction in UPCR compared with placebo at week 36 of a phase 3 trial. The FDA is scheduled to deliver a verdict on the med in IgAN by Nov. 30, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Vera estimates IgA nephropathy affects about 160,000 patients in the US with 5,000 new cases a year, and — using Otsuka's pricing for Voyxact — puts the US market at roughly $20 billion. Trutakna is a weekly self-administered autoinjector, versus once every four weeks for Voyxact and povetacicept.
key_facts.excerpt: Vera's conservative estimate has framed IgAN's prevalence at 160,000 patients in the U.S. and an incidence rate of 5,000 per year. ... Using Otsuka's pricing for Voyxact, Vera estimates the IgAN market is worth about $20 billion in the U.S. alone. ... Trutakna is administered via a self-administered autoinjector every week, whereas Otsuka's Voyxact and Vertex's povetacicept are both administered once every four weeks.

key_facts.fact: The FDA's own novel drug approvals list records the atacicept clearance on 7/7/2026 for reducing proteinuria in adults with primary IgA nephropathy at risk for disease progression.
key_facts.excerpt: 7/7/2026, To reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy at risk for disease progression.

stories.headline: New Jersey signs energy law taxing large data centers and credits 3.6M households

key_facts.fact: Governor Mikie Sherrill signed an 'energy affordability' package on Tuesday July 7 and announced $90 million in immediate ratepayer relief, including a $25 August bill credit for 3.6 million New Jersey residential electric customers and an extra $150 for low-income families.
key_facts.excerpt: Gov. Mikie Sherrill on Tuesday signed an "energy affordability" package and announced $90 million in immediate relief for ratepayers — including a $25 August bill credit for 3.6 million New Jersey residential electric customers and an additional $150 for low-income families.

key_facts.fact: The most contested of the three bills, S-731/A-796, imposes tariffs on large-load data centers and creates a retail program outside the PJM market through which a new large load can offset its capacity obligation by paying to reduce demand elsewhere on the system.
key_facts.excerpt: The third bill, S-731/A-796, sponsored by Senator John Burizichelli (D-3) and Assemblyman Bailey, would impose tariffs on large load data centers. The bill would also create a retail program—outside the PJM market—through which a new large load offsets its capacity obligation by paying to reduce demand elsewhere on the system

key_facts.fact: Sherrill justified the data-center tariff by pointing to grid data: 'New data centers use enormous amounts of power. Our grid operator, PJM said they drove 70% of new electricity demands last year. PJM isn't stopping them from driving up everyone else's cost, and I'm not going to wait for them to figure it out.'
key_facts.excerpt: "New data centers use enormous amounts of power," Sherrill said. "Our grid operator, PJM said they drove 70% of new electricity demands last year. PJM isn't stopping them from driving up everyone else's cost, and I'm not going to wait for them to figure it out."

key_facts.fact: The other two bills roll back incentives utilities receive simply for belonging to regional grid operator PJM, tighten oversight of costly transmission and infrastructure projects, and require utilities to prioritize advanced, lower-cost grid technologies.
key_facts.excerpt: The bills will roll back incentives that utilities have received for belonging to the regional grid operator PJM, tighten oversight of costly transmission and infrastructure projects, and require utilities to prioritize advanced, lower-cost grid technologies, the governor said.

key_facts.fact: According to consultancy Synapse Energy Economics, cited by Sherrill, the three bills would save New Jersey ratepayers over $1 billion annually.
key_facts.excerpt: Sherrill said the three bills would save New Jersey ratepayers over $1 billion annually, according to Synapse Energy Economics, a research and consulting firm.

key_facts.fact: The package was signed the same day as the announcement of the utility bill credits, in a state where the AI data-center buildout has become a live political issue over electricity prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Sherrill signs energy package, announces utility bill credits for 3.6 million customers - New Jersey Globe, July 7, 2026

stories.headline: Brazil sees 25% US tariff as near-inevitable as USTR opens hearings before July 15 deadline

key_facts.fact: Lula's government sees little chance of escaping the 25% US tariffs on Brazilian goods due to take effect from July 15, but considers it a priority to keep an open negotiating channel with the Trump administration.
key_facts.excerpt: O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vê pouca chance de escapar da aplicação de tarifas de 25% dos Estados Unidos sobre produtos brasileiros, a partir do dia 15 de julho, mas considera prioritário manter um canal aberto de negociações com a administração americana.

key_facts.fact: Brazilian government technicians met with USTR officials on Tuesday July 7, during the second day of hearings, and requested a further meeting with USTR chief Jamieson Greer before the July 15 decision date.
key_facts.excerpt: técnicos do governo brasileiro se reuniram nesta terça-feira (7) com representantes do USTR... Marcio Elias Rosa afirmou que a reunião deve ter continuidade ao longo da semana e que o governo brasileiro solicitou um novo encontro com Jamieson Greer, chefe do USTR.

key_facts.fact: The USTR proposes a 25% tariff based on alleged unfair competitive practices plus a further 12.5% over forced labour, a total of 37.5%. Development Minister Márcio Elias Rosa said cutting Brazil's import tax on US ethanol is not on the negotiating table.
key_facts.excerpt: o USTR é o órgão americano que propõe um novo tarifaço de 37,5% ao Brasil com base na acusação de práticas concorrenciais desleais (25%) e uso de trabalho forçado (12,5%). ... O ministro Márcio Elias Rosa (Desenvolvimento, Indústria e Comércio) rebateu nesta terça-feira (7) a proposta do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) de eliminar o imposto de importação do etanol americano

key_facts.fact: At the USTR public hearing, Brazilian exporters argued the tariffs would raise input costs for US industry and consumers; Amcham Brasil president Abrão Neto said the central point was showing the surcharges would hurt US competitiveness.
key_facts.excerpt: — O ponto central foi mostrar que a eventual aplicação de sobretaxas sobre importações brasileiras vai ter efeitos negativos para a própria economia americana em relação a aumento de custos e perda de competitividade do setor produtivo, que usa insumos, máquinas e equipamentos e produtos exportados pelo Brasil — contou Abrão Neto, presidente da Amcham Brasil

key_facts.fact: Of 78 entities and individuals registered to speak at the hearing, 63 opposed the tariffs and 15 supported them; among 34 Brazilians registered, only Senator Flávio Bolsonaro did not oppose the measures, instead proposing a postponement, according to the Presidency's communications office.
key_facts.excerpt: "Ao todo, 78 entidades e pessoas físicas se inscreveram para se manifestar sobre o tarifaço. Desse total (somando brasileiros e estadunidenses), 63 são contra o tarifaço, 15 são a favor. Das 44 intervenções de estadunidenses, 30 são contra o tarifaço e 14 a favor. Entre os 34 brasileiros inscritos, só Flávio Bolsonaro não se posicionou contrário às medidas contra o Brasil, optando por sugerir o seu adiamento, com claro objetivo eleitoreiro"

key_facts.fact: The USTR asked Brazil to cut import duties on cars, chemicals and pharmaceuticals without specifying which tariff lines; talks on critical minerals stalled after USA Rare Earths bought Brazilian miner Serra Verde in April.
key_facts.excerpt: O USTR chegou a pedir redução de alíquotas de importação no Brasil para carros, produtos químicos e farmacêuticos, mas sempre sem detalhar quais "linhas tarifárias"... Depois da compra da mineradora Serra Verde pela USA Rare Earths, em abril, o USTR não se engajou mais nas negociações.
